physics.electricity-charge-explain-kb.00.a: charge is conserved - not created or destroyed; all electrons entering must leave (rate of flow in = out)
physics.electricity-charge-explain-kb.00.b: same electrons flow through each part, only one path; electrons not used up, so rate of flow of charge is same everywhere
physics.electricity-charge-explain-kb.00.c: 1.5 J of energy transferred per coulomb of charge passing through the cell

physics.electricity-charge-recall-kb.000.a: charge = current x time (Q = I t)

physics.electricity-circuits-describe-kb.a: current increases but by smaller amounts as voltage increases (not proportional); curve levels off
physics.electricity-circuits-describe-kb.b: changing the resistor's resistance (slider moves, changes length of wire) - increasing resistance decreases current, decreasing resistance increases it

physics.electricity-circuits-explain-kb..a: total resistance increases so current decreases; voltage shared among more lamps so less power each
physics.electricity-circuits-explain-kb..b: current heats filament; temperature rises so metal ions vibrate more; electrons collide more often with ions so resistance increases

physics.electricity-circuits-extended-kb.b: LDR resistance high in dark; thermistor resistance high in cold; each in potential divider with fixed resistor; voltage across LDR/thermistor rises when dark/cold; this voltage operates a switch (transistor/relay) turning on lamps / heater; relay allows small sensor current to switch large mains current; adjust with variable resistor to set threshold

physics.electricity-circuits-recall-kb.0.b: if one lamp breaks the others stay on / each lamp gets full voltage so brighter / can be switched independently

physics.electricity-mains-describe-kb.00.a: fuse in live wire contains thin wire; if current exceeds rating, wire heats and melts; circuit broken so current stops, preventing overheating/fire
physics.electricity-mains-describe-kb.00.b: cell gives direct current (one direction, constant); mains is alternating current (direction reverses, 50 Hz, 230 V)
physics.electricity-mains-describe-kb.00.c: casing made of plastic insulator, live parts cannot touch an accessible conducting part; so case cannot become live - no earth wire needed

physics.electricity-mains-explain-kb.000.a: electrons collide with ions in the resistor lattice; transfer energy to ions, which vibrate more - thermal energy store increases
physics.electricity-mains-explain-kb.000.b: fuse melting disconnects appliance from the high voltage live wire; if in neutral, appliance would remain live after fuse blew, risk of shock

physics.electricity-mains-extended-kb.00.a: kettle; toaster (electric heater, hair dryer, iron)
physics.electricity-mains-extended-kb.00.b: I = P/V = 2000/230 = 8.7 A; choose fuse just above normal current: 13 A (3 A and 5 A would blow in normal use); too large a fuse would let dangerous current flow in fault without melting, wires overheat - fire; too small blows immediately

physics.electricity-mains-recall-kb.0002.all: earth wire; fuse (or circuit breaker / double insulation)

physics.electricity-static-explain-kb.00.a: friction transfers electrons from jumper to balloon; balloon gains electrons so has excess negative charge
physics.electricity-static-explain-kb.00.b: negative balloon repels electrons in wall surface away; surface of wall nearest becomes positive (induced charge); attraction between opposite charges (closer, stronger than repulsion) holds balloon
